title.es: Lo que dicen los buenos líderes

es: Reconocer en el habla de un entrenador si una frase es instrucción, ánimo o retroalimentación, y distinguir cuándo dirige y cuándo apoya.

teaching.en: A good coach will give instructions in short, clear sentences: pass the ball sooner and stay in your position.
teaching.es: Un buen entrenador da instrucciones en frases cortas y claras: pasa el balón antes y mantén tu posición.
teaching.explanationEs: Instrucción: imperativo directo que dice qué hacer ahora.
segments: A good coach will give instructions in short, clear sentences:
pass the ball sooner and stay in your position.
teaching.audioText: A good coach will give instructions in short, clear sentences: pass the ball sooner and stay in your position.

teaching.en: I love your effort today; you never gave up, and that is what will encourage the younger players most.
teaching.es: Me encanta tu esfuerzo de hoy; nunca te rendiste, y eso es lo que más animará a los jugadores más jóvenes.
teaching.explanationEs: Ánimo: reconoce el esfuerzo y motiva, sin dar órdenes.
segments: I love your effort today; you never gave up, and
that is what will encourage the younger players most.
teaching.audioText: I love your effort today; you never gave up, and that is what will encourage the younger players most.

teaching.en: Your strength is your speed, but your passes were late in the second half, so that is what we should improve.
teaching.es: Tu punto fuerte es la velocidad, pero tus pases llegaron tarde en la segunda parte, así que eso es lo que debemos mejorar.
teaching.explanationEs: Retroalimentación: un punto fuerte + un dato concreto + algo que mejorar.
segments: Your strength is your speed, but your passes were late in
the second half, so that is what we should improve.
teaching.audioText: Your strength is your speed, but your passes were late in the second half, so that is what we should improve.

teaching.en: Keep going, you are doing great under pressure, and I want you to shoot as soon as you see the space.
teaching.es: Sigue así, lo estás haciendo genial bajo presión, y quiero que dispares en cuanto veas el espacio.
teaching.explanationEs: Ánimo e instrucción pueden ir juntos: Keep going motiva y shoot dice qué hacer.
segments: Keep going, you are doing great under pressure, and I want
you to shoot as soon as you see the space.
teaching.audioText: Keep going, you are doing great under pressure, and I want you to shoot as soon as you see the space.

teaching.en: The coach gave us some feedback after the match: constructive criticism names one concrete thing and ends with a next step.
teaching.es: El entrenador nos dio algunos comentarios tras el partido: la crítica constructiva nombra una cosa concreta y termina con un siguiente paso.
teaching.explanationEs: Feedback no tiene plural: some feedback, a lot of feedback.
segments: The coach gave us some feedback after the match: constructive criticism
names one concrete thing and ends with a next step.
teaching.audioText: The coach gave us some feedback after the match: constructive criticism names one concrete thing and ends with a next step.

teaching.en: Before the final, the coach gave a short pep talk that made everybody feel calmer and more confident.
teaching.es: Antes de la final, el entrenador dio una breve charla de ánimo que hizo que todos se sintieran más tranquilos y seguros.
teaching.explanationEs: Una pep talk es una charla corta para motivar al equipo justo antes de competir.
segments: Before the final, the coach gave a short pep
talk that made everybody feel calmer and more confident.
teaching.audioText: Before the final, the coach gave a short pep talk that made everybody feel calmer and more confident.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál de estas frases es una instrucción directa del entrenador?

choices.text: Pass the ball sooner and stay in your position.
I love your effort; you never gave up today.
Your strength is your speed, but your passes were late.

feedback.es: La instrucción usa el imperativo (pass, stay) y dice qué hacer ahora; las otras animan o valoran.

hint.es: Busca la frase que empieza con un verbo en imperativo.

prompt.es: Completa: «Tu punto fuerte es tu velocidad, pero tus pases llegaron tarde.»

feedback.es: Strength es el punto fuerte: la retroalimentación útil empieza reconociendo lo que funciona.

hint.es: Es el sustantivo de «punto fuerte»; empieza por str-.

origin.text: The coach did not shout at the team. She simply told Mia: Your ___ is your speed, but your passes were late in the second half.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Sigue así, lo estás haciendo genial bajo presión.»

answer.text: Keep going you are doing great under pressure

feedback.es: Keep going y You are doing great motivan; under pressure cierra la frase.

hint.es: Empieza con Keep going y termina con under pressure.

prompt.es: Escucha la charla del descanso y elige qué función tiene «I love your effort today».

choices.text: It tells her exactly what to change in the second half.
It recognises her effort without giving her an order.
It gives her a fact about how the game is going.

feedback.es: «I love your effort» reconoce el esfuerzo de Mia sin dar órdenes ni datos: es ánimo.

origin.audio: At half-time, the coach spoke to the players. Pass the ball sooner, she told Leo, and stay in your position. Then she turned to Mia. I love your effort today, she said, you never gave up. Your strength is your speed, but your passes were late in the first half, so try looking up before you pass. The team was losing two to nothing, but nobody looked worried. Keep going, the coach added: you are doing great under pressure.

prompt.es: Con la misma charla, elige qué se le pide a Mia que haga distinto.

choices.text: To pass the ball sooner and stay in her position.
To shoot as soon as she sees the space.
To look up before she passes the ball.

feedback.es: La mejora para Mia es mirar antes de pasar; pasar antes y mantener la posición era la instrucción para Leo.

origin.audio: At half-time, the coach spoke to the players. Pass the ball sooner, she told Leo, and stay in your position. Then she turned to Mia. I love your effort today, she said, you never gave up. Your strength is your speed, but your passes were late in the first half, so try looking up before you pass. The team was losing two to nothing, but nobody looked worried. Keep going, the coach added: you are doing great under pressure.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del entrenador con su función.

pairs: Shoot as soon as you see the space.
You never gave up today, well done!
Your passes were late in the second half.

feedback.es: La instrucción dice qué hacer, el ánimo reconoce el esfuerzo y la retroalimentación describe un hecho concreto.

pairs: Shoot as soon as you see the space.
You never gave up today, well done!
Your passes were late in the second half.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué actitud adopta la entrenadora con el jugador.

choices.text: She supports him while giving one clear thing to work on.
She insists that the miss was bad luck and that nothing needs to change.
She praises his courage but avoids saying anything specific about the mistake.

feedback.es: Elogia su valentía y su esfuerzo y señala un único punto concreto: apoyo con una mejora clara.

origin.audio: After the match, the coach sat next to a player who had missed an easy chance. She did not raise her voice. You were brave to try to score, she said, and your effort was the best in the team. The decision was late, though, so next time try looking at the goal before you shoot. Then she smiled. I want you to shoot again on Saturday.

prompt.es: Con el mismo relato, elige por qué dice «I want you to shoot again on Saturday».

choices.text: To give him an order about his new position.
To show that she still trusts him after the mistake.
To warn him that he will be tested on Saturday.

feedback.es: Pedirle que vuelva a disparar demuestra confianza: el fallo no cambia lo que espera de él.

origin.audio: After the match, the coach sat next to a player who had missed an easy chance. She did not raise her voice. You were brave to try to score, she said, and your effort was the best in the team. The decision was late, though, so next time try looking at the goal before you shoot. Then she smiled. I want you to shoot again on Saturday.

prompt.es: Completa: «Prefieren la crítica constructiva: una cosa concreta y un siguiente paso.»

feedback.es: Constructive criticism es la crítica que señala un punto concreto y propone un siguiente paso.

origin.text: Good coaches avoid vague comments like That was bad. They prefer ___ criticism: one concrete thing and a next step.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Levanta la vista antes de pasar el balón.»

answer.text: Look up before you pass the ball

feedback.es: La instrucción va en imperativo y sitúa la condición con before.

prompt.es: Lee el mensaje del entrenador y elige con qué propósito lo escribe.

choices.text: To encourage the team and avoid talking about any mistakes.
To complain that the players do not run enough and to ask for extra running.
To give feedback that recognises a strength and proposes a next step.

feedback.es: El mensaje nombra un punto fuerte (correr), un dato concreto (pérdidas en el medio) y un paso siguiente: retroalimentación.

origin.text: Coach's message to the team: Good work tonight. I know you are tired. Your strength this season is how hard you run, but we lose the ball too often in the middle of the pitch. On Thursday, let's practise short passes. See you at six.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué quiere enseñar el entrenador con sus palabras.

choices.text: That clear, calm instructions help more than shouting does.
That players should never talk during training.
That only the coach is allowed to give instructions.

feedback.es: El entrenador sustituye el grito por frases claras y tranquilas: «Pass to me» en lugar de culpar.

origin.audio: During a training session, a young player kept shouting at his teammates. The coach stopped the practice and said quietly: Encourage, don't blame. When you shout, people get tense and pass the ball too fast. Next time, say what you need: I'm open, or Pass to me. Try it now.

prompt.es: Completa: «Sus comentarios nos mostraron cómo mejorar nuestros pases.»

feedback.es: Improve significa mejorar; la retroalimentación útil enseña en qué y cómo hacerlo.

origin.text: We were losing every game until the coach's comments showed us exactly how we could ___ our passing.

es: Formular preguntas de coaching abiertas e hipotéticas (What would it take to...?, What's stopping you from...?) en lugar de dar consejos directos.

teaching.en: A coach rarely gives advice; instead she asks, What would it take to reach a goal that you set for this month?
teaching.es: Un coach rara vez da consejos; en cambio pregunta: ¿qué haría falta para alcanzar una meta que te fijaste para este mes?
teaching.explanationEs: What would it take to + verbo: pregunta abierta sobre lo necesario.
segments: A coach rarely gives advice; instead she asks, What would it
take to reach a goal that you set for this month?
teaching.audioText: A coach rarely gives advice; instead she asks, What would it take to reach a goal that you set for this month?

teaching.en: What is the biggest obstacle for you right now, and which option feels more realistic given your week?
teaching.es: ¿Cuál es el mayor obstáculo para ti ahora mismo, y qué opción te parece más realista dada tu semana?
teaching.explanationEs: Pregunta abierta con What y Which: no se contesta con sí o no.
segments: What is the biggest obstacle for you right now,
and which option feels more realistic given your week?
teaching.audioText: What is the biggest obstacle for you right now, and which option feels more realistic given your week?

teaching.en: How would you feel if you could make progress this week, and what would make you more confident?
teaching.es: ¿Cómo te sentirías si pudieras avanzar esta semana, y qué te haría sentirte más seguro?
teaching.explanationEs: Pregunta hipotética: would + if + pasado simple (could).
segments: How would you feel if you could make progress
this week, and what would make you more confident?
teaching.audioText: How would you feel if you could make progress this week, and what would make you more confident?

teaching.en: What would you do if you were more confident, and what small first step could you take tomorrow morning?
teaching.es: ¿Qué harías si fueras más seguro de ti mismo, y qué pequeño primer paso podrías dar mañana por la mañana?
teaching.explanationEs: If + pasado simple (were) imagina un escenario; take a step = dar un paso.
segments: What would you do if you were more confident, and
what small first step could you take tomorrow morning?
teaching.audioText: What would you do if you were more confident, and what small first step could you take tomorrow morning?

teaching.en: What's stopping you from speaking in front of the group, and what might hold back your best ideas?
teaching.es: ¿Qué te impide hablar delante del grupo, y qué podría frenar tus mejores ideas?
teaching.explanationEs: What's stopping you from + -ing: busca el obstáculo real.
segments: What's stopping you from speaking in front of the
group, and what might hold back your best ideas?
teaching.audioText: What's stopping you from speaking in front of the group, and what might hold back your best ideas?

teaching.en: A good question can reveal a blind spot or push you out of your comfort zone, so ask it as a real option, not a hidden order.
teaching.es: Una buena pregunta puede revelar un punto ciego o sacarte de tu zona de confort, así que formúlala como una opción real, no como una orden encubierta.
teaching.explanationEs: Evita Why don't you...?: suena a pregunta, pero es un consejo disfrazado.
segments: A good question can reveal a blind spot or push you out of your
comfort zone, so ask it as a real option, not a hidden order.
teaching.audioText: A good question can reveal a blind spot or push you out of your comfort zone, so ask it as a real option, not a hidden order.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál de estas es una pregunta de coaching abierta, no un consejo ni un sí o no?

choices.text: Do you think you can reach your goal this month?
What would it take to reach a goal this month?
Why don't you just set a smaller goal this month?

feedback.es: Solo «What would it take…?» es abierta: no se responde con sí o no ni esconde un consejo.

hint.es: Descarta la que se responde con sí o no y la que suena a consejo.

prompt.es: Completa: «¿Qué te impide hablar delante del grupo?»

feedback.es: What's stopping you from + -ing busca el obstáculo real que frena a la persona.

hint.es: Es el verbo en -ing que va antes de you from.

origin.text: The player says that she wants to be more confident. Her coach answers with a question instead of advice: What's ___ you from speaking in front of the group?

prompt.es: Ordena: «¿Qué harías si fueras más seguro de ti mismo?»

answer.text: What would you do if you were more confident

feedback.es: La pregunta hipotética une would en la principal con el pasado simple (were) tras if.

hint.es: Empieza con What would you do y usa were tras if.

prompt.es: Escucha la sesión y elige qué hace la entrenadora en lugar de dar un consejo.

choices.text: She explains why mistakes are part of the game.
She warns him that the school team will not wait.
She asks questions that help him name his own problem.

feedback.es: La entrenadora pregunta en vez de aconsejar, y así él mismo nombra su problema (el miedo a equivocarse).

origin.audio: A volunteer coach was talking to a boy who wanted to join the school team but kept finding excuses. She did not tell him to try harder. Instead, she asked: What's stopping you from going to the first training? He said he was afraid of making mistakes in front of the others. So she asked another question: What would it take for you to feel more confident? After a pause he answered that he could ask a friend to come with him. The coach simply smiled.

prompt.es: Con la misma sesión, elige qué sugiere la sonrisa final de la entrenadora.

choices.text: That the idea came from him, which is exactly what she hoped for.
That she thinks his plan is too simple for him.
That she had already decided to invite his friend.

feedback.es: Sonríe porque la solución (llevar a un amigo) la encontró él: es lo que busca una pregunta de coaching.

origin.audio: A volunteer coach was talking to a boy who wanted to join the school team but kept finding excuses. She did not tell him to try harder. Instead, she asked: What's stopping you from going to the first training? He said he was afraid of making mistakes in front of the others. So she asked another question: What would it take for you to feel more confident? After a pause he answered that he could ask a friend to come with him. The coach simply smiled.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es más fácil hallar una solución cuando puedes nombrar el mayor obstáculo.»

feedback.es: Obstacle es lo que se interpone en el camino; nombrarlo es el primer paso de una buena pregunta de coaching.

origin.text: Most people already know part of the answer. It is easier to find a solution once you can name the biggest ___ in your way.

prompt.es: Escribe dos preguntas de coaching para que la jugadora se atreva a pedir ayuda.

answer.text: What's stopping you from asking your coach for help? What would it take for you to feel more confident?
accepted: What's stopping you from asking your coach for help? What would it take for you to feel more confident?
What is stopping you from asking him for help? What would it take to be more confident?
What's stopping you from asking for help? What would it take for you to feel more confident?

feedback.es: Dos preguntas abiertas, una sobre el obstáculo (What's stopping you from...?) y otra hipotética (What would it take...?), sin dar consejos.

origin.text: Una jugadora te dice: «Quiero pedirle ayuda a mi entrenador, pero me cuesta hacerlo.» No le des consejos. Escribe dos preguntas abiertas: una sobre lo que se lo impide (What's stopping you from...) y otra hipotética sobre lo que haría falta para sentirse más segura.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué funcionó mejor el segundo entrenador.

choices.text: The second coach set a more ambitious target than the first coach.
The player found her own solution instead of receiving orders.
The player trusted the second coach more because that coach was more experienced.

feedback.es: La jugadora encuentra su propia solución (usar el descanso); al primero solo le dieron órdenes y no hizo nada.

origin.audio: Two coaches talked to the same player. The first said: You should practise every day, and you should stop worrying. The player nodded but did nothing. The second asked: What would help you to practise three times this week? The player thought for a moment, then said she could use her lunch break. She wrote it down and looked surprised at how simple it was.

prompt.es: Con la misma escena, elige qué sugiere que la jugadora «looked surprised».

choices.text: That she disagreed with the question that the coach had asked.
That she was shocked by how much practice was needed.
That she had not expected to find an answer so easily.

feedback.es: La sorpresa se refiere a lo simple que era la solución, no al desacuerdo ni al esfuerzo requerido.

origin.audio: Two coaches talked to the same player. The first said: You should practise every day, and you should stop worrying. The player nodded but did nothing. The second asked: What would help you to practise three times this week? The player thought for a moment, then said she could use her lunch break. She wrote it down and looked surprised at how simple it was.

prompt.es: Completa: «¿Qué haría falta para hablar con ella?»

feedback.es: What would it take to + verbo es la pregunta abierta que sustituye al consejo disfrazado.

origin.text: Why don't you talk to her? sounds like a question, but it is really advice in disguise. A better version is: What would it ___ to talk to her?

prompt.es: Lee lo que dice el adolescente y elige la respuesta que es una pregunta de coaching.

choices.text: What's stopping you from finishing one small thing this week?
You should finish one small thing every week, starting today.
Why don't you ask a friend to check your work every day?

feedback.es: Solo «What's stopping you…?» es una pregunta abierta; las otras son consejos, aunque una suene a pregunta.

origin.text: A boy tells his coach: I never finish anything, and I do not know why.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige con qué fin hace la entrenadora la segunda pregunta.

choices.text: To reassure the youngest player that there is nothing to be nervous about.
To help the players turn their worry into something useful.
To move the conversation away from winning the match.

feedback.es: La segunda pregunta parte de la emoción de la jugadora y busca convertirla en algo útil, sin juzgarla.

origin.audio: At the end of the session, the coach asked the team: How would you feel if we won the next match? Nobody answered at first. Then the youngest player said that she would feel proud, but also nervous. The coach wrote both words on the board and asked: What would help us turn the nervous feeling into energy?

prompt.es: Completa: «¿Qué opción es más realista esta semana: una sesión larga o tres cortas?»

feedback.es: Realistic describe lo que se puede cumplir en la práctica; una buena pregunta ayuda a elegir una opción realista.

origin.text: You cannot do everything at once. Which option feels more ___ for you this week: one long session or three short ones?

es: Valorar si una retroalimentación es específica, respetuosa y accionable, y decidir qué habría que mejorar en las que no lo son.

vocabulary.es: accionable; que se puede poner en práctica

teaching.en: I noticed that you rushed your last two passes, which is a specific observation that anyone on the pitch could confirm.
teaching.es: Me fijé en que hiciste con prisa tus dos últimos pases, y esa es una observación concreta que cualquiera en el campo podría confirmar.
teaching.explanationEs: Específica: describe un hecho que se vio, no una opinión.
segments: I noticed that you rushed your last two passes, which is
a specific observation that anyone on the pitch could confirm.
teaching.audioText: I noticed that you rushed your last two passes, which is a specific observation that anyone on the pitch could confirm.

teaching.en: That was terrible, and you never listen to anybody: that kind of comment is disrespectful, and it does not tell you what to do next.
teaching.es: Eso fue terrible y nunca escuchas a nadie: ese tipo de comentario es irrespetuoso y no te dice qué hacer después.
teaching.explanationEs: Irrespetuosa: ataca a la persona con terrible y never, y no dice qué hacer.
segments: That was terrible, and you never listen to anybody: that kind of comment
is disrespectful, and it does not tell you what to do next.
teaching.audioText: That was terrible, and you never listen to anybody: that kind of comment is disrespectful, and it does not tell you what to do next.

teaching.en: Next time, breathe before you shoot and stay calm, because a steady start gives you more time to choose your shot.
teaching.es: La próxima vez, respira antes de disparar y mantén la calma, porque un comienzo sereno te da más tiempo para elegir tu tiro.
teaching.explanationEs: Accionable: Next time + imperativo = un paso que se puede dar.
segments: Next time, breathe before you shoot and stay calm, because a
steady start gives you more time to choose your shot.
teaching.audioText: Next time, breathe before you shoot and stay calm, because a steady start gives you more time to choose your shot.

teaching.en: I suggest you practise your left foot twice a week; that is an actionable step, because you can start it tomorrow.
teaching.es: Te sugiero que practiques tu pie izquierdo dos veces por semana; es un paso accionable, porque puedes empezarlo mañana.
teaching.explanationEs: I suggest you + verbo base: sugerencia concreta, sin to.
segments: I suggest you practise your left foot twice a week; that
is an actionable step, because you can start it tomorrow.
teaching.audioText: I suggest you practise your left foot twice a week; that is an actionable step, because you can start it tomorrow.

teaching.en: Your talk was helpful because you gave clear examples, and your respectful tone made it easy for the group to listen.
teaching.es: Tu charla fue útil porque diste ejemplos claros, y tu tono respetuoso hizo que al grupo le resultara fácil escuchar.
teaching.explanationEs: Valorar con un motivo: because + dato concreto.
segments: Your talk was helpful because you gave clear examples, and your
respectful tone made it easy for the group to listen.
teaching.audioText: Your talk was helpful because you gave clear examples, and your respectful tone made it easy for the group to listen.

teaching.en: "That was good, I guess" is only a vague comment, so ask politely: could you be more specific about what worked?
teaching.es: «Estuvo bien, supongo» es solo un comentario vago, así que pregunta con educación: ¿podrías ser más concreto sobre qué funcionó?
teaching.explanationEs: Ante un comentario vago, pide concreción con Could you be more specific?
segments: "That was good, I guess" is only a vague comment, so
ask politely: could you be more specific about what worked?
teaching.audioText: "That was good, I guess" is only a vague comment, so ask politely: could you be more specific about what worked?

prompt.es: ¿Qué comentario es específico y respetuoso a la vez?

choices.text: You always rush everything you do on the pitch.
That was not very good, but I am sure you will improve.
I noticed that you rushed your last two passes.

feedback.es: Solo el comentario sobre los dos últimos pases cita un hecho concreto sin juzgar a la persona.

hint.es: Busca el que cita un hecho que se vio, sin always ni never.

prompt.es: Completa: «“Estuvo bien, supongo” es un comentario vago: no dice qué repetir.»

feedback.es: Un comentario vago suena amable, pero no cita ningún hecho ni dice qué hacer.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo contrario a specific.

origin.text: That was good, I guess is a ___ comment: it does not tell you what to repeat or what to change.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La próxima vez, respira antes de disparar y mantén la calma.»

answer.text: Next time breathe before you shoot and stay calm

feedback.es: Next time + imperativo es la estructura de un paso accionable.

hint.es: Empieza por Next time y acaba con stay calm.

prompt.es: Escucha los comentarios del entrenador y elige cuál es específico y accionable.

choices.text: The one about the rushed passes and breathing before the next pass.
The one that says the talk was good, I guess.
The one that says that the player never listens to anybody at all.

feedback.es: Solo el segundo comentario cita un hecho (pases apresurados) y un paso que se puede dar (respirar antes de pasar).

origin.audio: After the tournament, three players received comments from their coach. To the first he said: That was terrible, you never listen. To the second he said: I noticed that you rushed your last two passes, so next time, breathe before you pass and stay calm. To the third he said: That was good, I guess. The third player looked confused and asked: Could you be more specific? The coach thought for a moment and answered: Your talk to the group was helpful because you gave clear examples.

prompt.es: Con los mismos comentarios, elige qué hace el tercer jugador para mejorar lo que recibe.

choices.text: He tells the coach that the comment was disrespectful.
He asks the coach to be more specific.
He accepts the comment and thanks the coach.

feedback.es: El tercer jugador pide concreción con «Could you be more specific?» y consigue un motivo claro.

origin.audio: After the tournament, three players received comments from their coach. To the first he said: That was terrible, you never listen. To the second he said: I noticed that you rushed your last two passes, so next time, breathe before you pass and stay calm. To the third he said: That was good, I guess. The third player looked confused and asked: Could you be more specific? The coach thought for a moment and answered: Your talk to the group was helpful because you gave clear examples.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada comentario con el criterio que incumple o cumple.

pairs: I noticed that you lost the ball three times.

feedback.es: El primero ataca a la persona, el segundo no cita ningún hecho y el tercero describe algo comprobable.

pairs: I noticed that you lost the ball three times.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué fue útil el comentario de Leo.

choices.text: It compared her presentation with the ones given by other volunteers.
It praised her for speaking quickly and clearly.
It described what he noticed and gave her a step to take.

feedback.es: Leo cita un hecho (habló rápido en el medio) y propone pasos (respirar, añadir un ejemplo): específico y accionable.

origin.audio: At the volunteer meeting, Sara gave a short presentation. Afterwards, her manager said: That was confusing. Leo, who was sitting next to her, tried again: I noticed that you spoke quickly in the middle, so next time, take a breath before each new idea, and it would help to add one example. Sara nodded.

It is disrespectful because it judges Sara as a person, not her presentation.
It is useful because it tells her to explain more.

feedback.es: «Confusing» expresa una impresión sin decir qué cambiar; no ataca a Sara ni propone un paso concreto.

prompt.es: Lee el correo y elige qué criterio incumple principalmente.

It is disrespectful: it judges Tom's attitude instead of describing facts.

origin.text: Email to a volunteer: Hi Tom, you were twenty minutes late, again. You clearly do not care about this project. Please fix this.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué da a entender la niña sobre el comentario «Try harder».

That it was too specific for a player of her age.
That it was vague and did not tell her how to improve.

origin.audio: A coach told a girl: Your start was fast, but you rushed the final part. Tomorrow, let's practise slowing down together. The girl smiled. At her old club, the coach only said: Try harder. She told her mother that this new feedback was the first that made her want to train.

prompt.es: Lee la situación y elige la versión mejorada del comentario «Good job».

choices.text: Good job: I noticed that you answered every question calmly; next time, add an example.
Good job, you are clearly the best speaker in the whole group, and everyone knows it.
Good job, but your answers were terrible in the middle.

feedback.es: La versión mejorada cita un hecho y propone un paso; las otras son elogio vago o ataque.

prompt.es: Escucha la charla y elige cómo abre la entrenadora su intervención.

choices.text: By pointing out the mistake that cost the match.
By recognising how the players feel about the loss.
By praising the captain for the goals that she scored.

feedback.es: Empieza con la emoción («the defeat hurts»); la crítica llega después con However.

origin.audio: The final whistle went, and the players sat in silence. The coach sat in front of them. I know the defeat hurts, she said, and you have every right to feel disappointed. Then she looked at the captain. Despite the defeat, I'm proud of how you defended in the second half. However, we lost the ball too often in the middle, and that is fixable. She paused. What will it take for us to bounce back next Saturday? Nobody answered, but a few players were already nodding.

prompt.es: Con la misma charla, elige qué sugiere que algunos jugadores asientan.

choices.text: They agree that the coach was unfair to the captain in the second half.
They believe that the defeat was nobody's fault.
They accept the challenge and start thinking about the next match.

feedback.es: Nadie responde, pero asentir indica que la pregunta les hace pensar en cómo recuperarse.

origin.text: Tu equipo perdió 3-2. Escribe una frase que reconozca un esfuerzo concreto (la velocidad en el ataque) y continúe con however y una crítica concreta (dejaron demasiado espacio atrás).

prompt.es: Escribe la charla del entrenador tras la derrota.

answer.text:
Team, sit down for a moment. I know this defeat hurts, and it is fine to feel disappointed. I feel the same.
First, I want to say what I saw. Despite the defeat, I'm proud of how you defended in the second half. Mia, your two tackles saved us three times, and Tom, you never stopped talking to the team. You deserve credit for that.
However, we lost the ball too often in the middle of the pitch, and that gave them the chance to score. It is only one thing, and it is fixable. One match does not decide our season.
So let me ask you: what would it take for us to keep the ball longer next Saturday? What could we try in training on Thursday? I would like to hear two ideas from each of you.
Go home, rest, and come back ready to learn. I believe in this team.
accepted:
Team, sit down for a moment. I know this defeat hurts, and it is fine to feel disappointed. I feel the same.
First, I want to say what I saw. Despite the defeat, I'm proud of how you defended in the second half. Mia, your two tackles saved us three times, and Tom, you never stopped talking to the team. You deserve credit for that.
However, we lost the ball too often in the middle of the pitch, and that gave them the chance to score. It is only one thing, and it is fixable. One match does not decide our season.
So let me ask you: what would it take for us to keep the ball longer next Saturday? What could we try in training on Thursday? I would like to hear two ideas from each of you.
Go home, rest, and come back ready to learn. I believe in this team.

Everyone, come here. I know how painful this defeat is, and I understand you are disappointed. I am too.
I want to start with what worked. I'm proud of how you supported each other during the last twenty minutes. Leo, your effort in defence was excellent, and Sara, you encouraged everybody until the final whistle.
However, we waited too long before we shot, and they blocked our chances easily. That is one concrete thing to improve, and it is not a disaster.
Now, what would help us to use the whole field next week? What is stopping us from looking for the right side? What could we try first on Tuesday? Think about it tonight, and tell me tomorrow.
It was a tough day, but you deserve to be proud of your effort. We will bounce back, and I will be with you on Saturday.

feedback.es: Una buena charla reconoce la emoción y dos esfuerzos concretos, hace una crítica específica con however y cierra con una pregunta de coaching.

origin.text: Tu equipo perdió 2–1 la final del barrio. prompt.es: Escucha el correo de la capitana y elige qué actitud muestra hacia la charla.

choices.text: She likes the talk but wants more concrete criticism too.
She values the talk, but she would prefer it to focus only on the positives.
She thinks the talk should have avoided any criticism.

feedback.es: La capitana agradece la charla pero pide más detalle sobre los errores: le gusta y exige concreción.

origin.audio: After the heavy defeat, the captain wrote an email to the coach. She said the talk had helped, but added that one sentence had stayed in her mind: It is only a setback. She explained that it had stopped her from blaming herself. In the same email she asked for more detail about the mistakes, because praise alone, she wrote, would not help the team improve.

prompt.es: Con el mismo correo, elige por qué menciona la frase «It is only a setback».

choices.text: Because it made her forget about the defeat entirely and stay calm.
Because it helped her stop blaming herself for the result.
Because it convinced her that nothing needed to change.

feedback.es: La frase la ayudó a dejar de culparse, pero ella sigue pidiendo detalles para mejorar: no olvidó la derrota.

choices.text: Criticism should always be avoided after a defeat.
Replacing the coach improves the results of the team.

title.es: Guiar a un equipo en el cambio

The garden will close earlier on Saturdays from next year.
More families are coming, so they need more time to welcome them.

feedback.es: La razón es que vienen más familias y hace falta más tiempo para recibirlas.

origin.audio: On Saturday morning, the coordinator of a community garden spoke to the volunteers to tell them about a change. Starting next month, she said, there will be two shifts instead of one, because more families are coming and we need more time to welcome them. She explained that each volunteer would choose a shift by Friday, and that a guide and a buddy would support anyone who felt unsure. One volunteer asked whether the early shift was required. The coordinator smiled and asked: What would make it easier for you to come in the morning?

prompt.es: Con el mismo anuncio, elige con qué propósito pregunta la coordinadora al voluntario.

choices.text: To involve the volunteer in finding a solution.
To check that he understands the new rules.
To persuade him to cancel his other plans.

feedback.es: La pregunta de coaching invita al voluntario a buscar una solución con ella, en lugar de imponerle una.

origin.audio: On Saturday morning, the coordinator of a community garden spoke to the volunteers to tell them about a change. Starting next month, she said, there will be two shifts instead of one, because more families are coming and we need more time to welcome them. She explained that each volunteer would choose a shift by Friday, and that a guide and a buddy would support anyone who felt unsure. One volunteer asked whether the early shift was required. The coordinator smiled and asked: What would make it easier for you to come in the morning?

prompt.es: Completa: «Quiero anunciar un cambio en nuestro horario de los sábados.»

feedback.es: Announce a change abre el mensaje de forma clara; no lleva persona directa (announce you).

origin.text: Thank you all for coming this morning. I want to ___ a change in our Saturday schedule, and I want to explain why.

prompt.es: Escribe el anuncio del cambio a los voluntarios.

answer.text:
Hi everyone,
Thank you for coming. I want to announce a change in our Saturday schedule. The reason is simple: more families are coming to the garden, and we need more time to help them.
Here is the plan. First, we will have two shifts instead of one: nine to twelve, and twelve to three. Second, each volunteer will choose a shift by Friday. Third, we will review the plan in a month.
We will support you with a clear guide and a buddy for your first week. Nobody will work alone.
Tom, I understand your concern about the early start. It sounds like you feel stressed because you study at night. What would make the afternoon shift easier for you?
Ana, I hear that you are worried about the new register. What would help you feel more confident? I can practise it with you on Thursday.
I know change is tough, but I am proud of what this team does every week. Thank you for your effort, and please tell me what you think.

We will support you with a clear guide and a buddy for your first week. Nobody will work alone.
Tom, I understand your concern about the early start. It sounds like you feel stressed because you study at night. What would make the afternoon shift easier for you?
Ana, I hear that you are worried about the new register. What would help you feel more confident? I can practise it with you on Thursday.
I know change is tough, but I am proud of what this team does every week. Thank you for your effort, and please tell me what you think.

Dear volunteers,
I want to announce a change for Saturdays. The reason is that many more families are coming to the garden, and our morning is now too short.
This is the plan. We will work in two shifts, one in the morning and one in the afternoon. Each of you can choose the shift that suits you best. We will review the schedule after four weeks, and then we will decide together if we keep it.
Of course, we will support you. You will receive a short guide, and an experienced volunteer will help you during the first week.
Tom, I understand your concern. You study at night, so the early start is hard. What would make the afternoon shift possible for you?
Ana, it sounds like you feel worried about the new register. What could we try so that you feel more confident? I am happy to practise it with you.
Change is never easy, but your effort makes a real difference. Thank you for your patience and your ideas.

feedback.es: Un buen anuncio da la razón, el plan y el apoyo, reconoce cada preocupación y responde con una pregunta de coaching.

origin.text: Eres coordinador de un huerto comunitario. Los sábados habrá dos turnos (9–12 y 12–15) porque vienen más familias. Tom estudia de noche y le preocupa el turno de la mañana; Ana teme no saber usar el nuevo registro. Escribe el anuncio (unas 220–270 palabras): razón del cambio, plan en pasos, apoyo y una respuesta con pregunta de coaching a cada preocupación.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué actitud adopta la coordinadora ante la queja de la voluntaria.

choices.text: She insists that the decision was made in a fair way.
She accepts the criticism of the process and asks for ideas.
She offers to cancel the change for this volunteer.

feedback.es: La coordinadora reconoce la queja («That is fair») y pide ideas: no defiende la decisión ni la cancela.

origin.audio: After the announcement, one volunteer stayed behind. I am not against the change, she told the coordinator, but nobody asked us before deciding. The coordinator did not defend the decision. She said: It sounds like you feel left out of the process, and you need to be heard earlier. That is fair. What would make it easier to give you a voice next time? The volunteer relaxed and said she would join the new shift.

prompt.es: Con la misma escena, elige qué se deduce del final de la conversación.

choices.text: She had only now realised that the change was really necessary.
She joined the new shift only because she had no choice.
Her concern was more about being heard than about the shift itself.

feedback.es: La voluntaria se relaja al sentirse escuchada y acepta el turno: su queja era sobre el proceso, no sobre el horario.

origin.audio: After the announcement, one volunteer stayed behind. I am not against the change, she told the coordinator, but nobody asked us before deciding. prompt.es: Completa: «La coordinadora intenta que cada voluntario se sume al plan.»

feedback.es: Get everyone on board significa conseguir que todos se sumen y apoyen el plan.

origin.text: The new plan will only work if the whole team supports it. The coordinator is trying to bring every volunteer on ___.

prompt.es: Lee el correo y elige qué incluye y qué omite el anuncio.

choices.text: It explains why, gives the plan and the support, but invites no concerns.
It gives the plan and the explanation, but offers no support at all.
It explains the plan and the support, but never says why.

feedback.es: El correo explica el porqué, da el plan y el apoyo (guía y compañero), pero no invita a expresar preocupaciones.

origin.text: Dear volunteers, from March the garden will open for two shifts on Saturdays, because many more families now visit us. You will receive a short guide, and a buddy will help you during your first week.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué cambió la actitud de la voluntaria.

choices.text: Getting the shift that she had wanted from the first day.
Feeling listened to when the coordinator asked what would help her.
Receiving a guide that explained the new schedule in detail.

feedback.es: Lo que cambió su actitud fue la pregunta de la coordinadora: sentir que su opinión contaba.

origin.audio: A new volunteer told her friend: At first I hated the two shifts. Then the coordinator said she understood my worry and asked what would help me. Nobody had ever asked me that. In the end I chose the afternoon, and I felt that my opinion counted. That single question turned my doubts into interest.

prompt.es: Completa: «Antes del plan, explica siempre el motivo del cambio.»

feedback.es: The reason for the change va antes del plan: quien entiende el porqué acepta mejor el cómo.

origin.text: People accept a new schedule more easily when they understand why. Before you present the plan, always explain the ___ for the change.
